title: A name change that reverts on reload
question: A user changes their display name, the page reloads, and it shows the old name. A second reload shows the new one. What is the right fix?
context: Writes go to the primary; all reads go to two asynchronous read replicas behind a load balancer. Replication lag is usually under a second.

options.label: Make replication synchronous so every replica has the write
options.why: It fixes the symptom by making every write wait for every replica, so one slow or unreachable replica now stalls writes for the whole product. That is a large price for one user seeing their own change.

options.label: Add more replicas so each one carries less load and lags less
options.why: Lag comes from applying the primary's changes, not from read load alone, and asynchronous replicas will always be some distance behind. More replicas make the window smaller at best; they cannot close it.

options.label: Read from the primary for that user for a few seconds after a write
options.why: This gives read-your-writes consistency where it matters — to the person who just wrote — and leaves everyone else on the replicas. The window only needs to cover normal lag; tracking the write position and waiting for a replica to reach it is the stricter version of the same idea.

options.label: Put profiles in Redis and update the cached copy on every single write
options.why: Now there are two copies that can disagree. A reader that misses the cache still lands on a lagging replica and may put the old name back in, which is harder to see than the bug you started with.
